### Lust for Power
Author: Stuart Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/lust-for-power-one-year-devotions-for-men-august-22.html
Passage: Judges 9:14-15
Points:
- The natural desire for personal freedom frequently twists into a corrupting ambition to dominate others.
- Abimelech exploited ethnic ties and used hired violence to eliminate rivals and seize control.
- Jotham courageously told a fable exposing Abimelech as a useless thornbush incapable of offering true shelter.
- Pursuing power over people inevitably plunges human hearts into oppression and destruction.
- The only safeguard against the corrupting lure of dominance is surrendering to God's reign.

### When You’ve Got a Bramble for a King
Author: Jared C. Wilson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/when-youve-got-a-bramble-for-a-king/
Passage: Judges 9:7-15
Points:
- Jotham indicts Israel's rejection of God's rule through personified fruit-bearing trees and a destructive bramble.
- The olive tree, fig tree, and grapevine refuse to abandon their God-given fruitfulness for worldly control.
- Choosing the thornbush illustrates how human idolatry chases wealth, superficial security, and presumed favor.
- Abimelech's promised shade is an illusion that conceals dangerous fire inside his reign.
- Christ is the true Vine who offers everlasting refuge, while every worldly substitute proves to be a bramble.
